title: Integral constructible complexes are compact
statement:
Work in the standing setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: $\ell$ is a prime, $k$ is a field of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and $X$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. Fix an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$. Regard $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ as the condensed ring of [def-sfb-padic-integers-condensed-ring] and put $R_X=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. All module sheaves are module objects over this ring [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and all derived categories, Hom and Ext groups are in the ordinary unbounded category $D(\Mod_{R_X})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category; def-pc-ext], without imposing derived completeness on arbitrary objects or completing their direct sums. Write $\Cons=\Cons(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and $\Dbc=\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Use canonical truncations with $H^q(K[s])=H^{q+s}(K)$ [def-kun-truncations]. All diagrams and families are small in the fixed universe [def-weil-size-convention; def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

Use $\operatorname{Ind}(\Cons)$ for formal small filtered diagrams $(C_i)$ of constructible sheaves, with morphisms $\varprojlim_i\varinjlim_j\Hom(C_i,D_j)$ (equivalently the filtered-colimit-of-representables category described in [lem-sfb-ind-filtered-colimits]). Choose $d_C\ge0$ for each $C\in\Cons$ satisfying the bound of [sk-lem-int-ext](2), enlarging a bound to zero when necessary. Then:

1. The realization $\Phi:\operatorname{Ind}(\Cons)\to\Mod_{R_X}$, $(C_i)\mapsto\varinjlim_i C_i$, is exact and fully faithful. Its essential image $\IndCons$ is the full subcategory of sheaves isomorphic to small filtered colimits of constructible sheaves. This image is closed under extensions and under kernels and cokernels of its own morphisms. For $C\in\Cons$ and $B\in\IndCons$, $\Ext^q(C,B)=0$ whenever $q>d_C$.
2. The full subcategory $\Dic=\{K\in D(\Mod_{R_X}):H^n(K)\in\IndCons\text{ for every }n\in\mathbf Z\}$ is closed under direct sums and canonical truncations and contains $\Loc(\Dbc)$, the smallest full triangulated subcategory containing $\Dbc$ and closed under isomorphisms and small direct sums [det-def-localizing-closure-existence]. For every $C\in\Cons$, $K\in\Dic$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical truncation zigzag induces a natural isomorphism
$$\Hom(C,K[m])\simeq\Hom(C,(\tau_{\ge m-d_C}\tau_{\le m}K)[m]).$$
3. Every $C\in\Dbc$ is compact in $\Loc(\Dbc)$ [def-pc-compact-object]: for every small family $(K_\alpha)$ in this localizing subcategory the canonical map
$$\bigoplus_\alpha\Hom(C,K_\alpha)\longrightarrow\Hom(C,\bigoplus_\alpha K_\alpha)$$
is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\Mod_{R_X}$ and $\mathcal H=\Cons$. The equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] identifies these internal modules with ordinary sheaves of modules over the section-ring sheaf of the same $R_X$; it preserves underlying abelian sheaves and section groups. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] gives all small colimits and exact filtered colimits in $\mathcal A$. By [sk-lem-int-integral-heart](1), $\mathcal H$ is essentially small, abelian with its ambient kernels and cokernels, and closed under extensions; its sheaves lie in $\Dbc$. Choose a small skeleton when forming Ind. By [sk-lem-int-ext](1), for each $C\in\mathcal H$ and every integer $q$, $\Ext^q(C,-)$ commutes with small filtered colimits of sheaves: the representing complexes are all concentrated in degree zero, so have common lower bound zero. In particular Hom and $\Ext^1$ have this continuity; in degree zero, $\Hom_{D(\mathcal A)}(C[0],B[0])=\Hom_{\mathcal A}(C,B)$ for sheaves $C,B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], so this is continuity of $\Hom_{\mathcal A}(C,-)$ itself. These are the integral hypotheses required below.

source.place: Paragraph (1), the three integral inputs; Stacks Tag 079Q (injectives-remark-existence-D) for the ambient category

proof.text:
For filtered diagrams $(C_i),(D_j)$ in $\mathcal H$, the colimit universal property and step 1 give
$$\Hom_{\mathcal A}(\varinjlim_i C_i,\varinjlim_jD_j)=\varprojlim_i\Hom_{\mathcal A}(C_i,\varinjlim_jD_j)=\varprojlim_i\varinjlim_j\Hom_{\mathcal H}(C_i,D_j).$$
These identifications send a represented morphism to its realization and respect identities and composition. By the defining Ind Hom formula in the statement, $\Phi$ is fully faithful, with exactly the stated essential image. We also need its colimit behavior. For arbitrary $M\in\mathcal A$, let $F_M(C)=\Hom_{\mathcal A}(C,M)$. If an ind-object $P$ is represented by $(C_i)$, then
$$\Hom_{\mathcal A}(\Phi P,M)=\varprojlim_i F_M(C_i)=\operatorname{Nat}(P,F_M).$$
The last equality is the presheaf colimit universal property: a natural map $h_C\to F_M$ is determined by its value at $1_C$, and its value at $t:T\to C$ is that element composed with $t$; these are inverse assignments. For a filtered diagram $(P_j)$, [lem-sfb-ind-filtered-colimits] computes its Ind colimit in presheaves. The displayed equality then identifies maps $\Phi(\varinjlim_j P_j)\to M$ with compatible families of maps $\Phi P_j\to M$. Thus $\Phi$ preserves filtered colimits by the colimit universal property, and $\IndCons$ is closed under filtered colimits in $\mathcal A$.

source.place: Paragraph (1), full faithfulness and realization; Stacks Tag 05PW (categories-remark-ind-category) Hom formula

proof.text: The image is also closed under arbitrary small sums. For a finite family of filtered presentations, take their product index category and the pointwise finite direct sum of the presented constructible sheaves. This index is filtered: choose common targets in each of the finitely many coordinates, and equalize parallel arrows coordinatewise. A cocone from these finite sums to $M$ is exactly one compatible cocone from each component diagram to $M$; hence its colimit is the finite direct sum of their realizations. The empty sum is the zero constructible sheaf. For an arbitrary family $(B_s)$ in the image, its direct sum is the filtered colimit over finite subsets $T$ of the finite sums $\bigoplus_{s\in T}B_s$: a cocone on these finite sums is precisely a family of maps $B_s\to M$. Apply step 2's filtered-colimit closure.

source.place: Paragraph (2), closure of IndCons under direct sums

proof.text:
Let $u:B\to B'$ be a morphism between objects of $\IndCons$. Lift it by the full faithfulness in step 2 and apply [lem-sfb-ind-arrow-presentation]. After isomorphisms of source and target, $u=\varinjlim_i u_i$ for one small filtered diagram of morphisms $u_i:C_i\to D_i$ in $\mathcal H$; step 2 identifies the realized source, target and arrow with these ambient colimits. Since filtered colimits in $\mathcal A$ are exact, taking the filtered colimits of the pointwise kernel-image-cokernel exact sequences gives
$$\ker u\simeq\varinjlim_i\ker u_i,\qquad\operatorname{coker}u\simeq\varinjlim_i\operatorname{coker}u_i.$$
All the terms on the right are constructible by step 1. Thus the full image is closed under ambient kernels and cokernels. It is additive by step 3 and is abelian: its kernels and cokernels are the ambient ones, and the ambient coimage-to-image isomorphism remains an isomorphism in the full image. Its inclusion is exact. Transport this structure through the fully faithful essentially surjective $\Phi$ to conclude that the realization of $\operatorname{Ind}(\mathcal H)$ is exact.

source.place: Paragraph (1), kernels, cokernels, and exactness of realization

proof.text: Consider $0\to N\to M\to B\to0$ in $\mathcal A$ with $N,B\in\IndCons$, and choose filtered presentations $N=\varinjlim_iD_i$, $B=\varinjlim_a C_a$ in $\mathcal H$. For each $a$, let $M_a=M\times_B C_a$; it fits into $0\to N\to M_a\to C_a\to0$. This is the dual of [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-short-exact-sequence], applied in $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}$; the axioms in [def-sp-abelian] are self-dual. Its class in $\Ext^1(C_a,N)$, interpreted by [lem-coef-yoneda-derived-ext-comparison], comes by step 1 from a class in $\Ext^1(C_a,D_i)$ for some $i$. An element of a filtered colimit of abelian groups is represented at a single stage, since it is a finite sum of stage elements and filteredness moves a finite sum to one common stage. Represent that class by $0\to D_i\to T\to C_a\to0$. Then $T\in\mathcal H$ by its extension closure. The pushout $N\amalg_{D_i}T$ is an extension of $C_a$ by $N$, by the pushout node, and its class is the class of $M_a$ by naturality of the Yoneda comparison. Consequently it is isomorphic to $M_a$ as an extension: a zigzag identifying Yoneda classes consists in degree one of maps with identity endpoints, whose middle maps are isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-short-five-lemma].

source.place: Paragraph (1), extension closure, expanded finite-stage extension lift; Stacks Tags 010I (homology-section-extensions), 06XU (derived-lemma-yoneda-extension), 06XV (derived-lemma-ext-1)

proof.text: For the index $i$ chosen for a fixed $a$ in step 5, use the undercategory $i/I$ of arrows $i\to j$. It is small and filtered: to find a common target, first find a common target of $j,j'$ in $I$ and then equalize the two resulting arrows from $i$; parallel arrows are equalized in $I$. The diagram $i\to j\mapsto D_j$ has colimit $N$: a cocone extends uniquely to $I$ by sending any $D_k$ through a common target of $k$ and $i$, with independence obtained by taking a further common target and equalizing the two maps from $k$ and from $i$. Put $P_{i\to j}=D_j\amalg_{D_i}T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-short-exact-sequence], $0\to D_j\to P_{i\to j}\to C_a\to0$ is exact, so $P_{i\to j}$ is constructible by step 1. Its colimit is $N\amalg_{D_i}T$: a compatible family $P_{i\to j}\to W$ amounts to a map $N\to W$ and a single map $T\to W$ agreeing on $D_i$ (the undercategory has initial object $1_i$, and the transition on $T$ is the identity). The pushout universal property identifies precisely such pairs. Hence $M_a\in\IndCons$.

source.place: Paragraph (1), extension closure, pushout presentation over i/I; Stacks Tag 010I (homology-section-extensions)

proof.text: The maps $M_a\to M$ form a compatible cocone by uniqueness in the pullback universal property. Take the filtered colimit over $a$ of $0\to N\to M_a\to C_a\to0$. Exactness from step 1 gives $0\to N\to\varinjlim_a M_a\to B\to0$; the colimit of the constant identity $N$ diagram is $N$, since the index is nonempty and connected. The canonical map to the original sequence has identity endpoint maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-short-five-lemma], $\varinjlim_a M_a\simeq M$. Step 2 and step 6 show that $M\in\IndCons$. This proves the remaining extension-closure assertion in (1).

source.place: Paragraph (1), extension closure, final filtered colimit

proof.text: For $C\in\mathcal H$ and $B=\varinjlim_iD_i$ with $D_i\in\mathcal H$, step 1's continuity identifies $\Ext^q(C,B)$ with $\varinjlim_i\Ext^q(C,D_i)$. By [sk-lem-int-ext](2), each term is zero when $q>d_C$, proving the uniform vanishing in (1). We will also use continuity for direct sums of arbitrary sheaves: express a sum as the filtered colimit of its finite partial sums as in step 3 and apply [sk-lem-int-ext](1), with all complexes in degree zero. Since finite sums are biproducts, $\Ext^q(C,\bigoplus_s B_s)=\bigoplus_s\Ext^q(C,B_s)$ for every integer $q$. Negative Ext vanishes by standard t-structure orthogonality [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category; def-weil-t-structure].

source.place: Paragraphs (1) and (3), uniform Ext bound and direct-sum continuity

proof.text: A long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] of a triangle $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ with $K,L\in\Dic$ gives a short exact sequence $0\to\operatorname{coker}(H^nK\to H^nL)\to H^n(M)\to\ker(H^{n+1}K\to H^{n+1}L)\to0$. Steps 4 and 7 put both endpoints and their extension in $\IndCons$. Cohomology of a shift is merely reindexed, so rotations give the other two-out-of-three cases; zero and isomorphisms cause no change. Thus $\Dic$ is triangulated. It is closed under truncations because the formulas [def-kun-truncations] retain or kill each cohomology sheaf. Direct sums are termwise coproducts by [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts], applied to the Grothendieck category of step 1. A direct sum is a filtered colimit of finite biproducts, so exact filtered colimits make it exact; consequently kernels, images, and their quotients in each degree commute with sums, and $H^n(\bigoplus_sK_s)=\bigoplus_sH^n(K_s)$. Step 3 puts this in $\IndCons$. By [sk-lem-int-integral-heart](1), every cohomology sheaf of an object of $\Dbc$ is constructible, hence is in $\IndCons$ through its constant filtered presentation. The minimality in [det-def-localizing-closure-existence] now gives $\Loc(\Dbc)\subseteq\Dic$.

source.place: Paragraph (2), direct sums, truncations, and localizing inclusion; Stacks Tags 07D9 (injectives-lemma-derived-products), 0118 (homology-section-truncations)

proof.text: Fix $C\in\mathcal H$ and $d=d_C$. First prove the lower-tail assertion $\Hom(C,L)=0$ for bounded $L\in\Dic$ with $H^qL=0$ for $q>-d-1$. Induct on the finite number of possibly nonzero cohomology degrees. The zero object gives the base case. Removing the highest remaining degree $q$ by the canonical truncation triangle [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle; def-kun-truncations] gives a layer $H^q(L)[-q]$. Its Hom from $C$ is $\Ext^{-q}(C,H^qL)=0$ by step 8 since $-q>d$. The exact Hom sequence [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] and the inductive hypothesis give $\Hom(C,L)=0$. This uses only the ambient Ext bound for ind-constructible sheaves, not compactness.

source.place: Paragraph (2), bounded lower tail; finite-window proof paragraph 2; Stacks Tags 08J5 (derived-remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), 0149 (derived-lemma-representable-homological)

proof.text:
Now let $L\in\Dic$ satisfy the same upper bound, without a lower bound. Put $L_n=\tau_{\ge-n}L$. Each $L_n$ is bounded, so $G_n=\Hom(C,L_n)=0$ by step 10. By [det-pe-left-complete-iso] and [det-pe-products-derived], valid for the sheaf of rings $R_X$ through step 1's module equivalence, $L\simeq\operatorname{Cone}(1-T:\prod_nL_n\to\prod_nL_n)[-1]$. Apply exact Hom to this triangle and its shifts [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact]. A map into a product is exactly its family of components, so this gives
$$\operatorname{coker}(1-T:\prod_n A_n\to\prod_n A_n)\longrightarrow\Hom(C,L)\longrightarrow\ker(1-T:\prod_n G_n\to\prod_n G_n),\quad A_n=\Hom(C,L_n[-1]),$$
with exactness and the left map injective. The right group is zero. The successive-truncation triangle has first term $H^{-n-1}(L)[n+1]$, middle $L_{n+1}$ and third $L_n$. After shifting by $-1$, exact Hom puts $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ between $\Ext^n(C,H^{-n-1}L)$ and $\Ext^{n+1}(C,H^{-n-1}L)$. Thus this transition is an isomorphism for $n>d$ by step 8. The cokernel on the left is zero: choose $N>d$. To solve $x_n-t_nx_{n+1}=a_n$ for an arbitrary $(a_n)$, set $x_N=0$, recursively set $x_{n+1}=t_n^{-1}(x_n-a_n)$ for $n\ge N$, and then set $x_n=a_n+t_nx_{n+1}$ for $n<N$ downwards. Hence $1-T$ is surjective and $\Hom(C,L)=0$. This is the missing unbounded-tail argument; no continuity assumption for unbounded systems is made.

source.place: Paragraph (2), left completeness and Milnor argument; finite-window proof paragraphs 3-4; Stacks Tag 0149 for Hom exactness

proof.text:
For arbitrary $K\in\Dic$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$, put $A=\tau_{\le m}K$, $U=\tau_{\ge m+1}K$, $V=\tau_{\le m-d-1}A$, $W=\tau_{\ge m-d}A$. The two truncation triangles [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle] are $A\to K\to U\to A[1]$ and $V\to A\to W\to V[1]$. Standard orthogonality [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category; def-weil-t-structure] gives $\Hom(C,U[m-1])=\Hom(C,U[m])=0$, since these objects lie in degrees at least $2$ and $1$. Step 9 puts $V[m],V[m+1]$ in $\Dic$; their upper degrees are $-d-1$ and $-d-2$, so step 11 gives zero Hom from $C$. Exact Hom [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] therefore makes both canonical arrows
$$\Hom(C,K[m])\ \longleftarrow\ \Hom(C,A[m])\ \longrightarrow\ \Hom(C,W[m])$$
isomorphisms. The resulting isomorphism is natural: for a morphism $K\to K'$ the truncation maps give commutative squares for both arrows, and composing the right square with the inverse of the left square preserves commutativity. This proves (2), with the stated degrees $[m-d_C,m]$.

source.place: Paragraph (2), finite-window isomorphism, explicit upper and lower truncation maps; Stacks Tags 08J5, 0149

proof.text:
For $C\in\mathcal H$ and a family $(M_s)$ with cohomology in one finite interval $[a,b]$, choose representing complexes and apply $\tau_{\ge a}\tau_{\le b}$; these are quasi-isomorphic representatives supported in that common interval by [def-kun-truncations]. The filtered diagram of finite partial sums has common lower bound $a$, and its termwise colimit is the termwise direct sum. The latter represents the derived direct sum by [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts]. Apply [sk-lem-int-ext](1) to this diagram, with the source $C\in\Dbc$ from step 1. It gives
$$\Hom(C,(\bigoplus_sM_s)[m])=\varinjlim_{T\subset S,\ T\text{ finite}}\Hom(C,(\bigoplus_{s\in T}M_s)[m])=\bigoplus_s\Hom(C,M_s[m]).$$
The last equality is the finite-biproduct identity followed by the finite-partial-sum universal property. All comparison maps are induced by the actual coprojections. This supplies the finite-range continuity used in paragraph (3) directly; it does not require the family to be bounded below outside this finite-range step.

source.place: Paragraph (3), continuity on a common finite cohomological interval

proof.text: Let $(K_s)$ be any small family in $\Loc(\Dbc)$, hence in $\Dic$ by step 9. For fixed $C\in\mathcal H$ and $m$, set $W_s=\tau_{\ge m-d_C}\tau_{\le m}K_s$. Exactness of sums in step 9 and the explicit kernel/cokernel formulas [def-kun-truncations] identify $\tau_{\ge m-d_C}\tau_{\le m}(\bigoplus_sK_s)$ canonically with $\bigoplus_sW_s$; both truncation maps commute with the coprojections. Apply the natural window isomorphisms of step 12 to each $K_s$ and to their sum, and step 13 to the family $(W_s)$ in its common interval $[m-d_C,m]$. The resulting commutative comparison square has isomorphisms on its vertical sides and on its finite-window horizontal side. Its other horizontal side is the canonical direct-sum comparison for $C$. It is therefore an isomorphism. Taking $m=0$ proves compactness of each constructible sheaf in the localizing category. This includes arbitrary shifts and families with no common lower bound.

source.place: Paragraph (3), pass from the finite window to arbitrary families

proof.text: Finally, [sk-lem-int-integral-heart](1) says that every $C\in\Dbc$ is bounded and its standard truncations remain in $\Dbc$ with constructible cohomology. Successive truncation triangles [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle; def-kun-truncations] therefore build $C$ by finitely many extensions of the shifts $H^q(C)[-q]$ of constructible sheaves, starting from zero. Work inside $\Loc(\Dbc)$, which is a full triangulated category with the same coproducts by [det-def-localizing-closure-existence]. Compact objects there are stable under shifts and distinguished triangles by [lem-sc-compact-objects-thick] (Stacks Tag 09QH). Step 14 and finite induction through these triangles show that $C$ is compact. This proves (3).

source.place: Paragraph (3), bounded-source truncation and stability of compact objects; Stacks Tag 09QH (derived-lemma-compact-objects-subcategory)

split_report.summary: Expanded the integral proof instead of applying rational-only nodes or nonexisting umbrella ids. Made inherited scheme/coefficient conventions explicit. Added two generic Mathlib leaves for ind filtered colimits and arrow presentations; all geometric and homological argument remains in the item. Proved extension closure via finite-stage Yoneda extensions and pushouts, checked both truncation tails with the Hom Milnor cokernel solved explicitly, and proved direct-sum comparison through the natural finite window. No target weakening or new geometric hypothesis.

tool_uses.why: Identifies internal module objects with modules over the same section-ring sheaf so ringed-site tools apply without changing coefficients.
Ambient small colimits and exact filtered colimits, a categorical input not supplied by the integral unit.
Generic abelian pushout and its dual pullback preserve short exact sequences, needed for the integral extension construction.
Classifies degree-one derived Ext by actual short exact sequences, needed to lift an extension along integral Ext continuity.
Identifies the middle objects of short exact sequences with isomorphic endpoints.
Generic cohomology long exact sequence proves the ambient ind-cohomology category is triangulated.
Computes ordinary unbounded derived coproducts termwise for any Grothendieck abelian category.
Generic localizing-closure definition and minimality, valid explicitly for every condensed coefficient ring.
Generic canonical truncation triangles, needed to expand the unit finite-window and bounded-source arguments.
Generic exact Hom sequences, needed for both tail vanishings and window isomorphisms.
Left completeness is stated for every ring sheaf, including the integral R_X; supplies the precise truncation-limit map.
Termwise products in the ambient derived category for any ring sheaf, needed for the Hom Milnor calculation.
Generic shift and triangle stability of compact objects completes finite source devissage.
